doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Alec Wilder and the Blue Angel
title: Meeting Alec Wilder at Sarah Churchill's apartment
summary: Rogers Brackett takes them to audition for Alec Wilder, whose 'oh, no' means approval, in Sarah Churchill's apartment.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And during that time our friend Alec Wilder entered the scene. We met him through a friend. We were working in New York City. And this friend of ours, who is Rogers Brackett, who is in advertising, said, “listen, I’d like Alec Wilder to hear you, because you’re doing some wonderful things now.” And he said, “could you come to this apartment, it’s on Central Park South?” Okay, sure. So we walk in and here’s this sumptuous apartment overlooking Central Park, and here’s a little piano over there and pictures on it and everything, and Alec is there and we meet him, and we talked and finally he said well do a couple of things. Alec sat down in a sofa with his back to us. Now I see how smart that was, he didn’t have to register anything. And we did this one song, we did “Lover.” It starts in three-four and then it goes [scats], and just piano, just piano, Jackie and I. And we did, we finished it, a great big ending and yeah, and all we hear from Alec is like, “oh, no.”
Oh, no, oh, no. Which was his sign of approval.
It’s like saying “oh, wow.” So then we understood — oh yes — okay, he was the first guy that said you’re bad.

Yeah. And he had a way of always remarking, like if you’d start something or do something that caught his ear, he’d go, “oh no, no” or something like that. It was weird. It was kind of strange but it was wonderful once we understood. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

And we were sitting at the piano and starting to relax a little bit, and we did about six, seven songs, and I keep looking at this picture in front of me on the piano. And I look and look, and it’s Winston Churchill and his wife, and someone standing behind them — his daughter Sarah. So we were in Sarah Churchill’s apartment, because Alec Wilder knew her and Rogers Brackett knew her, and we could use the apartment to meet Alec while she was out of town. I said, wow, seeing Winston Churchill and Alec at the same day, woooh.
